no_answer.scope:
Measure note over-returning and the recall cost of fixed output caps.

Caps are post-hoc diagnostics, not production filters or latency measurements.
Captured evaluation data must identify its capture and independent label owner;
authored negative controls must not be presented as independent real queries.

truncation.scope:
Controlled local reranker ablation on frozen, already-delivered passages.

This measures model input visibility and conditional ranking, not retrieval or
answer quality. Labels never enter the Rust scorer's input. No remote calls.

truncation_diagnosis.scope: Post-hoc diagnosis only; any-window is an oracle upper bound, tail is the last 32 non-trailing-whitespace bytes, not a new gold label. No new model calls.

protocol.scope: Full pinned trees; source delivery only. No independent production queries or answer-quality labels.

limits: Authored controls and source-derived questions are not independent production queries.
No generated-answer quality evaluation or controlled latency comparison.
Source-delivery completeness and note relevance precision are separate metrics.
Relative HTTP route links are host-unknown inferences, not deployed-host proof; absolute URLs require matching known origins.
Route extraction remains opt-in; existing immutable graph episodes require rebuilding or a new episode to acquire route facts.
Small packet budgets enforce bounds but cannot promise all requested evidence fits.
Default single-repository nexus-update-identity remains a known baseline miss; the full HTTP trial uses explicit retrieval settings.
The final note replay precedes the identity-only digest cache; all six negatives were rerun with the cached-identity binary and the final accepted note guards.
